findings.explanation: The persistent, storage-backed idempotency guard (storage.tryMarkMid, keyed on Facebook's mid, no TTL — bounded only by MID_LIMIT eviction, backed by a unique DB constraint in postgres-adapter.js or a Set in file-adapter.js) only runs when `mid` is truthy (guarded at webhook.js:661 `if (mid) {`). `mid` is read exclusively from `event.message.mid`. Facebook postback events (button clicks, persistent-menu taps — event.postback.payload, handled at webhook.js:756) and pure referral events (m.me / ads click-to-Messenger — event.referral, handled via handleReferralOnly at webhook.js:761-765) never carry a `message` object, so `mid` is always undefined for them and they skip the dedup block entirely. These paths fall back only to short-lived, in-process, non-persistent guards: a 5s text-match cache (MESSAGE_TEXT_DEDUPE_TTL_MS, webhook.js:26) for postback payloads, or a 15s menu cooldown (MENU_SEND_COOLDOWN_MS, webhook-queue.js irrelevant — defined webhook.js:28) for referral-triggered menu sends. When Meta re-delivers a webhook because the 200 response wasn't received in time (a well-documented real-world occurrence, and the exact scenario reported in production here), any retry landing after these short windows — or on a different app instance if horizontally scaled, since the Maps are per-process — will be processed and sent to the customer a second time. Only text/quick_reply message events with a real `mid` get durable, cross-restart, cross-instance protection.
